svg.title: Skala after step 10: sensor mounting assembly schematic
svg.desc: Three-quarter and right-side views of the two fixed tracks, retained chassis and deck, OpenCR, Pi with WM8960 HAT, raised LiDAR bridge and front camera pan/tilt head. Colours identify new sensor mounts. The interface board and power installation remain unfinished.

g.text: Skala — after Step 10
Sensor mounts fitted • fixed-track prototype • camera facing forward
ASSEMBLY SCHEMATIC
U2 candidate / 07 Nov 2026
FRONT-RIGHT VIEW
FRONT
RPLidar A1
Above the bridge on four 35 mm columns.
Owned scanner must match the A1 drawing.
New side frames and LiDAR bridge.
Load goes into the retained deck.
WM8960 Audio HAT
On the Pi; microphone openings stay clear.
Pillar stack depends on seated header gap.
Raspberry Pi 4B + P10
Under the HAT, toward the front.
USB / Ethernet connectors face robot-left.
OpenCR + P9
At the rear of the upper deck.
Retained board adapter and supports.
Camera 3 + P13–P16
Front pan/tilt head, at its centre pose.
Passive pivot captured by wall and washer.
P6 deck + P5 chassis
Retained plates and 60 mm deck columns.
No replacement of these parts required.
Two fixed track modules
Two brackets support each carrier.
No pitch articulation at this stage.
RIGHT SIDE
READING THIS VIEW
Teal = new printed sensor mounts
Grey = retained structure • Green = circuit boards
P17 sits below the bridge at the rear; its interface-board
attachment is still unresolved. The board is not shown fitted.
ASSEMBLY STATE
Unpowered sensor-fit candidate.
A1 housing, Pi, servos and sprockets simplified.
Cable / small-fastener detail omitted for clarity.
Power hardware and final harness: steps 11–12.
Current CAD proportions • placement view, not a drilling template • actual hardware matching and cable sweep still required
